context:
Fill the routing seam from the head-to-head item. Reuse the basis bar, the run-card anatomy and the Top-N limiter from that item rather than duplicating them, and reuse the existing QueryHeatmap grid semantics -- role=grid, roving tabindex, sticky columns -- rather than building a second heatmap.

Baseline selection is the organising choice: every ratio, the standings order and the Top-N filters are relative to it, and switching it must re-base everything consistently.

Hold the same-query-set rule at the layout level. With four runs the chance that some query is missing a pass on at least one run is materially higher than with two, so the standings must state the size of the query set every geomean was computed over.
description:
A three or four run comparison is a ranking problem, not a diff. The current page answers it with the two-run layout: a flat QueryDiffTable emitting one row per (query x non-baseline candidate), which for four runs over 103 TPC-DS queries is 309 rows with no ordering and no way to see which runs disagree.

The approved design gives the multi-run selection its own layout behind the routing seam added by the head-to-head item: run cards with a baseline radio, one shared measurement basis, a six-axis identity matrix showing which axes vary across all runs rather than just between two, a diverging query-by-run heatmap of ratios against the baseline, and a standings table ordered by geomean with queries-won.

The heatmap is the load-bearing piece. It reads polarity -- faster or slower than baseline -- so it uses a two-hue diverging scale with a neutral midpoint, and every cell carries its ratio as text so colour is never the only encoding.

anti_patterns.dont: Build a fresh heatmap component because the existing one is large and platform-shaped.
anti_patterns.instead: Extend QueryHeatmap, keeping its grid semantics and keyboard model.
anti_patterns.why: That component carries accessibility behaviour earned over several remediation passes; a fresh grid would silently drop roving tabindex and sticky-column handling.

anti_patterns.dont: Encode a run's identity by colour alone in the heatmap columns.
anti_patterns.instead: Label every column with engine and hardware directly.
anti_patterns.why: The heatmap's colour channel is already carrying ratio polarity. Reusing it for identity would collide two encodings in one channel.

anti_patterns.dont: Let each run's geomean use whatever queries that run recorded.
anti_patterns.instead: Intersect across all selected runs first and state the resulting query count.
anti_patterns.why: With four runs the probability that some query is incomplete somewhere is high, and per-run query sets would make the standings order an artefact of coverage rather than speed.

anti_patterns.dont: Render 309 rows of per-query detail below the heatmap for completeness.
anti_patterns.instead: Let the heatmap carry per-query detail and apply the Top-N limiter to its rows.
anti_patterns.why: The flat table at four-run scale is the specific failure this layout exists to replace.

anti_patterns.dont: Use a rainbow or multi-hue scale for the ratio heatmap because it shows more gradation.
anti_patterns.instead: Use two hues with a neutral midpoint, one for faster than baseline and one for slower.
anti_patterns.why: The quantity has a meaningful zero -- parity with the baseline. A rainbow destroys the polarity reading and is unreadable for colour-vision-deficient users.

preserves.behavior: All three or four run selections must keep resolving through the existing /results/compare route and ?ids= grammar; MAX_COMPARE_SELECTIONS stays at 4.
Every geomean in the standings must be computed over the same query set, and the standings must state that set's size.
Every heatmap cell must carry its ratio as text so colour is never the sole encoding.
Existing comparability guardrails and claim suppression must fire in this layout exactly as in the two-run layout.
Switching the baseline must re-base every ratio, the heatmap and the standings consistently; no panel may keep a stale baseline.
The heatmap must keep QueryHeatmap's existing grid accessibility: role=grid, roving tabindex, sticky first columns and keyboard navigation.
The single shared basis rule holds identically here: N runs, exactly one basis, enforced by the model.
chartMath parity with the Python ASCII chart implementation must continue to pass.

prior_art.concept: Existing 862-line platform-by-query matrix with role=grid, roving tabindex, sticky left columns and per-cell hue/lightness custom properties. Extend it for a diverging baseline-ratio scale rather than writing a second heatmap.
Existing query-by-platform ordinal rank table with a win-count footer. Reuse its win-counting semantics for the standings table.
Existing parity test binding chart maths to the Python implementation. Any chartMath change must keep it passing or extend it deliberately.

colorForCell and lightnessForCell already implement the heatmap scale maths and are parity-tested against the Python ASCII output. Extend with the diverging variant in the same place so parity is maintained.
Owns the categorical palette and the diverging tokens the heatmap must use. Reuse; do not introduce new colour values.
